prs.author: rxits
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport.close() does not settle in-flight JSON-response-mode POST requests: handleRequest()'s Promise<Response> is only resolved by send(), and close() tears down the stream mapping without resolving it, leaving the HTTP request hanging until the platform's own timeout fires (and the caller unable to tell if a mutating call actually ran). (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: WebStandardStreamableHTTPServerTransport.close() does not settle in-flight JSON-response-mode POST requests: handleRequest()'s Promise<Response> is only resolved by send(), and close() tears down the stream mapping without resolving it, leaving the HTTP request hanging until the platform's own timeout fires (and the caller unable to tell if a mutating call actually ran). (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Both PRs edit the same close() path in packages/server/src/server/streamableHttp.ts to resolve pending JSON-mode response promises instead of leaving them hanging. #2600's diff has broader scope: beyond settling pending POSTs, it also clears `_requestToStreamMapping` (previously left populated after close()), and adds a re-check in send() after the `eventStore.storeEvent()` await so a response computed after close() doesn't get recorded against a retired correlation — a distinct leak (dangling correlations/responses for the process lifetime) that #2692's changeset does not mention or address. #2692's fix is scoped only to the pending-POST-hang case, using per-request-id JSON-RPC -32000 errors grouped by stream rather than #2600's single 404. Keeping #2600 covers the superset of the underlying close()-cleanup problem; #2692's narrower response-shaping can be reconciled on top of it if desired.

members.cluster_pick_reason: #2763 ships a changeset (this monorepo requires one for release notes; #2817 has none) and fixes both halves of the bug: it caps the initial arm at min(timeout, maxTotalTimeout) for the no-progress case and re-arms on progress against the remaining budget. #2817 only adds `info.startTime = Date.now()` inside the progress-reset path without capping the delay — resetting the elapsed-time baseline on every progress ping undoes the hard-cap guarantee #2763 establishes, since repeated progress notifications would keep pushing the deadline out indefinitely. The two changes are incompatible if merged together, not additive.
